0.title: Help My Unbelief
0.overview:
Many Christians struggle with doubt, and many feel ashamed to admit it. They wonder whether God is really there, whether the Bible is really true, whether they are really saved, or why God seems silent when they pray. Some keep their doubts hidden for years, fearing what others would think. Some drift away from the faith because no one helped them.

Scripture is surprisingly honest about doubt. The Psalms are full of questions. John the Baptist, in prison, sent to ask Jesus whether he really was the one. Thomas refused to believe without seeing. A desperate father cried out to Jesus, I believe; help my unbelief! (Mark 9:24). And Jesus did not turn any of them away.

Doubt is not the same as unbelief. Doubt is faith struggling; unbelief is faith refused. A believer can doubt and still belong to Christ, because salvation rests not on the strength of our faith but on the strength of the Saviour we trust. Even weak faith in a strong Christ saves.

Five units: (1) Honest Doubt in Scripture; (2) Kinds of Doubt; (3) When God Seems Silent; (4) Unanswered Prayer; (5) Strengthening Faith. The Apologetics study addresses intellectual questions about the faith in more depth.

1.title: Honest Doubt in Scripture
1.overview:
Believers who questioned. The Bible does not hide the struggles of God's people. Habakkuk cried out, O LORD, how long shall I cry for help, and you will not hear? (Hab 1:2). Asaph almost slipped when he saw the wicked prosper (Ps 73:2-3). Gideon asked for sign after sign (Judg 6). Elijah, after his greatest victory, sat under a tree and asked to die (1 Kgs 19:4). These were not unbelievers. They were saints whose faith was tested.

John the Baptist. John had baptised Jesus, seen the Spirit descend and called him the Lamb of God. But in Herod's prison, waiting for death, he sent his disciples to ask, Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another? (Matt 11:3). Jesus did not rebuke him. He sent back evidence: the blind see, the lame walk, the dead are raised, the poor hear good news. Then he praised John to the crowd (Matt 11:11).

The father of the boy. A man brought his son, tormented by an evil spirit, to Jesus. He said, if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us. Jesus answered, "If you can"! All things are possible for one who believes. The father cried, I believe; help my unbelief! (Mark 9:22-24). Jesus healed the boy. Mixed faith, honestly brought to Jesus, was enough.

Thomas. Thomas refused to believe the resurrection unless he could touch Jesus' wounds. A week later, Jesus appeared and invited him to do exactly that. Thomas confessed, My Lord and my God! (John 20:28). Jesus met Thomas in his doubt and led him to the highest confession in the Gospels.

Mercy for doubters. Jude tells the church, And have mercy on those who doubt (Jude 22). Doubting believers need patience, not condemnation.
1.theology:
Doubt and unbelief: Scripture warns against an evil, unbelieving heart that falls away from God (Heb 3:12). That is the settled refusal to trust. Doubt is different: it is a mind and heart torn between faith and fear. The doubter still turns to God with questions. The unbeliever turns away.

Faith is trust: Faith is not a feeling of certainty, but trust in God and his promises. One can trust while feeling uncertain, as a nervous patient trusts a surgeon.

The object of faith: What saves is not the size of our faith but its object. A small faith in Christ unites us to him as truly as a great faith. Jesus said that faith like a grain of mustard seed is enough (Matt 17:20).
1.examples:
Then: After Jesus walked on water, Peter asked to come to him. He stepped out and walked, but when he saw the wind he became afraid and began to sink. He cried, Lord, save me. Jesus immediately reached out his hand and took hold of him (Matt 14:30-31). Peter doubted, but he cried out, and Jesus caught him.

Now: A woman who has been a Christian for twenty years confesses to her small group that she has had serious doubts for months. She fears they will be shocked. Instead, two others admit they have struggled too. They study the Psalms together and pray for each other. Her faith does not return overnight, but she is no longer alone.

A simple test: Have you ever been afraid to admit your doubts to another Christian? Why?

verseByVerse.quote: And they brought the boy to him. And when the spirit saw him, immediately it convulsed the boy, and he fell on the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth. And Jesus asked his father, "How long has this been happening to him?" And he said, "From childhood. And it has often cast him into fire and into water, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us." And Jesus said to him, "'If you can'! All things are possible for one who believes." Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, "I believe; help my unbelief!" And when Jesus saw that a crowd came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, "You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and never enter him again." And after crying out and convulsing him terribly, it came out, and the boy was like a corpse, so that most of them said, "He is dead." But Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him up, and he arose. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The father's request was half faith and half doubt. Jesus picked up his words: If you can! The issue was not Jesus' ability but the man's trust. The father's honest cry, help my unbelief, is a prayer every believer can pray. Jesus answered it by healing his son.

verseByVerse.quote: Now when John heard in prison about the deeds of the Christ, he sent word by his disciples and said to him, "Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?" And Jesus answered them, "Go and tell John what you hear and see: the blind receive their sight and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them. And blessed is the one who is not offended by me." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: John in prison wondered whether he had been wrong. Jesus answered with the evidence of his works, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecies. Then he added a gentle word: blessed is the one who is not offended by me. Jesus does not always do what we expect, but he is still the one.

verseByVerse.quote: Now Thomas, one of the twelve, called the Twin, was not with them when Jesus came. So the other disciples told him, "We have seen the Lord." But he said to them, "Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, and place my finger into the mark of the nails, and place my hand into his side, I will never believe." Eight days later, his disciples were inside again, and Thomas was with them. Although the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace be with you." Then he said to Thomas, "Put your finger here, and see my hands; and put out your hand, and place it in my side. Do not disbelieve, but believe." Thomas answered him, "My Lord and my God!" Jesus said to him, "Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Thomas demanded proof. Jesus gave it, inviting him to touch his wounds. Thomas believed and worshipped. Then Jesus blessed those who believe without seeing. That includes us. We have the testimony of those who saw, written so that we may believe (John 20:31).

verseByVerse.quote: O LORD, how long shall I cry for help, and you will not hear? Or cry to you "Violence!" and you will not save? Why do you make me see iniquity, and why do you idly look at wrong? Destruction and violence are before me; strife and contention arise. So the law is paralyzed, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked surround the righteous; so justice goes forth perverted. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Habakkuk complains that God is not listening and not acting against injustice. The law is paralysed and justice never goes forth. This is a prophet speaking, in Scripture. God allows honest complaint and answers it, as the rest of the book shows.

1.reflection:
Which biblical example of doubt do you identify with most? Why?

What is the difference between doubt and unbelief?

How did Jesus respond to doubters? What does that tell you about him?

Is there someone you know who is struggling with doubt? How could you show them mercy?

2.title: Kinds of Doubt
2.overview:
Doubt comes in different forms, and each needs a different kind of help.

Intellectual doubt. Some doubts are questions about evidence and arguments. Is the Bible reliable? Did Jesus really rise? Why does God allow suffering? How does faith relate to science? These questions deserve honest answers. Christianity is not afraid of questions. Luke wrote his Gospel that you may have certainty concerning the things you have been taught (Luke 1:4). Peter said, we did not follow cleverly devised myths (2 Pet 1:16). Good books, wise teachers and patient study help.

Emotional doubt. Some doubts are driven by feelings, not arguments. In depression, grief, anxiety or exhaustion, God can feel unreal or far away, even when we know the truth. The psalmist speaks to his own soul: Why are you cast down, O my soul? (Ps 42:5). Emotional doubt needs rest, care, honest lament and the reminder that feelings are not facts.

Doubt from suffering. Some doubts arise from pain: a child's death, a long illness, an injustice. Why would a loving God allow this? These doubts need comfort before arguments. Job's friends tried to explain; Job needed God himself.

Doubt about salvation. Some believers doubt not God but themselves. Am I really saved? Have I committed the unforgivable sin? Is my faith real? These doubts need the gospel: salvation rests on Christ's finished work, not on the strength of our feelings. The Assurance of Salvation study addresses this.

Doubt from sin. Sometimes doubt is a cover for something else. A person who wants to live in sin may find reasons to doubt God's word. Jesus said, If anyone's will is to do God's will, he will know whether the teaching is from God (John 7:17). Honest self-examination is part of dealing with doubt.
2.theology:
Mind and heart: Faith involves the whole person: mind, heart and will. Doubts may arise in any of these. Help must address the right part.

The Spirit's witness: Ultimately, certainty about God comes not from arguments alone but from the Spirit's work. The Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God (Rom 8:16). Arguments can remove obstacles; the Spirit gives conviction.

The community of faith: Doubt grows in isolation. The church carries its members' faith when they cannot carry it themselves. Hebrews calls believers to exhort one another every day (Heb 3:13).
2.examples:
Then: Asaph, in Psalm 77, could not sleep and felt that God had rejected him. Has his steadfast love forever ceased? (Ps 77:8). Then he deliberately remembered God's deeds, especially the exodus (Ps 77:11-20). Memory of God's past faithfulness strengthened his faith for the present.

Now: A university student begins to doubt the resurrection after a sceptical lecture. A Christian friend gives her a careful book on the evidence and studies 1 Corinthians 15 with her. Her questions are taken seriously, and over time her faith becomes stronger than before, because it has been tested.

A simple test: If you have doubts, what kind are they: intellectual, emotional, from suffering, about salvation or from sin?

verseByVerse.quote: Inasmuch as many have undertaken to compile a narrative of the things that have been accomplished among us, just as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word have delivered them to us, it seemed good to me also, having followed all things closely for some time past, to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, that you may have certainty concerning the things you have been taught. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Luke carefully investigated everything from the beginning, using eyewitness accounts, and wrote an orderly account so that Theophilus might have certainty. Christianity is grounded in history and evidence. Faith is not a leap in the dark.

verseByVerse.quote: For we did not follow cleverly devised myths when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty. For when he received honor and glory from God the Father, and the voice was borne to him by the Majestic Glory, "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased," we ourselves heard this very voice borne from heaven, for we were with him on the holy mountain. And we have the prophetic word more fully confirmed, to which you will do well to pay attention as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts, knowing this first of all, that no prophecy of Scripture comes from someone's own interpretation. For no prophecy was ever produced by the will of man, but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter insists that he and the apostles did not follow myths. They were eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty at the transfiguration. Beyond that, we have the prophetic word, more fully confirmed, which came from God through men carried along by the Holy Spirit. Our faith rests on eyewitness testimony and inspired Scripture.

verseByVerse.quote: "Will the Lord spurn forever, and never again be favorable? Has his steadfast love forever ceased? Are his promises at an end for all time? Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has he in anger shut up his compassion?" Selah Then I said, "I will appeal to this, to the years of the right hand of the Most High." I will remember the deeds of the LORD; yes, I will remember your wonders of old. I will ponder all your work, and meditate on your mighty deeds. Your way, O God, is holy. What god is great like our God? You are the God who works wonders; you have made known your might among the peoples. You with your arm redeemed your people, the children of Jacob and Joseph. Selah (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Asaph asks six painful questions: Will the Lord spurn forever? Has his steadfast love ceased? Has God forgotten to be gracious? Then he chooses to remember the deeds of the LORD. He meditates on God's wonders and his redemption of his people. Remembering is a weapon against doubt.

verseByVerse.quote: About the middle of the feast Jesus went up into the temple and began teaching. The Jews therefore marveled, saying, "How is it that this man has learning, when he has never studied?" So Jesus answered them, "My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me. If anyone's will is to do God's will, he will know whether the teaching is from God or whether I am speaking on my own authority. The one who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory; but the one who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and in him there is no falsehood. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Jews marvelled at Jesus' teaching. He said his teaching came from the one who sent him, and that anyone who wants to do God's will will know whether it is from God. Willingness to obey opens the way to understanding. Sometimes doubt is resolved by surrender, not only by study.

2.reflection:
Which kind of doubt do you struggle with most?

How does Luke 1:1-4 show that Christianity is grounded in history?

Read Psalm 77. How did remembering help Asaph?

Is there any area where your doubts might be connected to an unwillingness to obey?

3.title: When God Seems Silent
3.overview:
One of the hardest experiences in the Christian life is when God seems absent. Prayers seem to hit the ceiling. Bible reading feels dry. There is no sense of God's presence. Many believers have walked through such seasons.

The psalmists knew it. How long, O LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me? (Ps 13:1). Psalm 88 ends without any resolution: my companions have become darkness (Ps 88:18). God included these prayers in Scripture so that we would know we are not alone, and so that we would have words to pray when we have none.

Walking in darkness. Isaiah gives counsel for such times: Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? Let him who walks in darkness and has no light trust in the name of the LORD and rely on his God (Isa 50:10). Notice that the person here fears God and obeys, yet walks in darkness. Darkness is not proof of God's displeasure. The answer is not to wait for feelings, but to trust God's name and lean on him.

Job's experience. Behold, I go forward, but he is not there, and backward, but I do not perceive him. Yet Job could also say, But he knows the way that I take; when he has tried me, I shall come out as gold (Job 23:8, 10). Job could not see God, but he believed God could see him.

Keep using the means. In dry seasons, keep praying, reading Scripture, attending church and taking the Lord's Supper, even when it feels empty. Feelings often return later. Meanwhile, the means of grace are doing their quiet work.

Christ was forsaken. On the cross, Jesus cried, My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? (Matt 27:46). He experienced the ultimate abandonment so that his people never will. When God seems silent to us, we can remember that he was truly silent to his Son, for our sake. And he promised, I will never leave you nor forsake you (Heb 13:5).
3.theology:
God's presence and our feelings: God is always present with his people (Matt 28:20). Our sense of his presence varies. Believers have long spoken of seasons when God seems to withdraw the felt sense of his nearness, to test and deepen faith. His actual presence never leaves.

Spiritual dryness and other causes: Dry seasons may come from tiredness, illness, depression, unconfessed sin or simply God's mysterious purposes. Wise counsel helps discern which.

Faith that does not depend on sight: For we walk by faith, not by sight (2 Cor 5:7). Faith that continues in darkness is precious to God.
3.examples:
Then: In Psalm 13, David moves in six verses from How long? to But I have trusted in your steadfast love (Ps 13:5). Nothing in his circumstances is said to have changed. His decision to trust came before his feelings changed.

Now: A missionary who has served faithfully for decades goes through a long season in which God feels distant. She keeps praying the Psalms, even when they feel empty. She tells a friend, "I can't feel him, but I know he's there." Years later, she describes that season as the time her faith grew deepest.

A simple test: If God feels distant right now, which psalm could you pray as your own?

verseByVerse.quote: How long, O LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me? How long must I take counsel in my soul and have sorrow in my heart all the day? How long shall my enemy be exalted over me? Consider and answer me, O LORD my God; light up my eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death, lest my enemy say, "I have prevailed over him," lest my foes rejoice because I am shaken. But I have trusted in your steadfast love; my heart shall rejoice in your salvation. I will sing to the LORD, because he has dealt bountifully with me. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: David asks How long? four times. He feels forgotten, abandoned and in danger. He asks God to answer and give light. Then, with no explanation, he turns: But I have trusted in your steadfast love. He resolves to sing. Lament can lead to trust, even before circumstances change.

verseByVerse.quote: Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? Let him who walks in darkness and has no light trust in the name of the LORD and rely on his God. Behold, all you who kindle a fire, who equip yourselves with burning torches! Walk by the light of your fire, and by the torches that you have kindled! This you have from my hand: you shall lie down in torment. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Isaiah addresses those who fear the LORD but walk in darkness. They are to trust the LORD's name and rely on him. Then he warns against lighting our own fires, making our own light rather than waiting on God. In darkness, the temptation is to find substitutes. The answer is to trust.

verseByVerse.quote: "Behold, I go forward, but he is not there, and backward, but I do not perceive him; on the left hand when he is working, I do not behold him; he turns to the right hand, but I do not see him. But he knows the way that I take; when he has tried me, I shall come out as gold. My foot has held fast to his steps; I have kept his way and have not turned aside. I have not departed from the commandment of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my portion of food. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Job searches in every direction and cannot find God. But he knows that God knows his way. When God has tested him, he will come out as gold. And he has treasured God's words more than his daily food. Job held to God's word when he could not feel God's presence.

verseByVerse.quote: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour. And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" that is, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Darkness covered the land as Jesus hung on the cross. He cried out with the opening words of Psalm 22, asking why God had forsaken him. The Son experienced real abandonment as he bore our sin. Because he was forsaken, God promises never to forsake his people.

3.reflection:
Have you experienced a season when God seemed silent? What helped you?

Read Psalm 88. Why do you think God included a psalm with no happy ending?

What does Isaiah 50:10 tell you to do in darkness?

How does Christ's cry of abandonment on the cross comfort you?

4.title: Unanswered Prayer
4.overview:
Few things shake faith like unanswered prayer. A believer prays for healing, and the person dies. A couple prays for a child for years, and none comes. A parent prays for a prodigal, who never returns. Where is God?

God always hears. And this is the confidence that we have toward him, that if we ask anything according to his will he hears us (1 John 5:14). God hears every prayer of his children. But he answers according to his will, which is wiser than ours.

Sometimes the answer is no. Paul prayed three times for his thorn to be removed. God said no, and gave something better: My grace is sufficient for you (2 Cor 12:9). Even Jesus, in Gethsemane, prayed let this cup pass from me, and the answer was no. Yet he added, nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will (Matt 26:39). The greatest prayer ever refused brought about our salvation.

Sometimes the answer is wait. Abraham waited twenty-five years for Isaac. Hannah prayed for years for a child (1 Sam 1). Jesus told a parable to the effect that they ought always to pray and not lose heart (Luke 18:1). Delay is not denial.

Sometimes the answer is different. God may answer in ways we do not recognise at first. We ask for comfort and he gives strength; we ask for removal and he gives endurance.

Sometimes we ask wrongly. You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, to spend it on your passions (Jas 4:3). Some prayers are not answered because they are selfish or contrary to God's will.

God works all things for good. And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose (Rom 8:28). This does not mean all things are good, but that God weaves even our disappointments into his good purpose: making us like Christ (Rom 8:29).
4.theology:
False teaching on prayer: Some teach that if we have enough faith, God must give us health and wealth. This is not biblical. Paul had great faith and was not healed. Faith trusts God's will; it does not command him.

Prayer and sovereignty: God has ordained that he will accomplish many things through the prayers of his people (Jas 5:16). Prayer is real and powerful. But it is always subject to his wiser will.

Lament as prayer: When prayers go unanswered, Scripture permits lament: honest complaint brought to God. Lament is still prayer, still faith, still turning to God rather than away.
4.examples:
Then: Hannah prayed so earnestly in the temple that the priest thought she was drunk. She poured out her soul. God answered, and she bore Samuel. Her song of praise afterwards is one of the great prayers of Scripture (1 Sam 2:1-10).

Now: A couple prayed for years for their son's healing, but he died young. Their faith was shaken. Over many months, through lament, the support of their church and the promise of resurrection, they came to trust God again. They still do not know why. But they know who, and they believe they will see their son again.

A simple test: Is there an unanswered prayer that has shaken your faith? Have you brought that disappointment honestly to God?

verseByVerse.quote: So to keep me from becoming conceited because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations, a thorn was given me in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to harass me, to keep me from becoming conceited. Three times I pleaded with the Lord about this, that it should leave me. But he said to me, "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me. For the sake of Christ, then, I am content with weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and calamities. For when I am weak, then I am strong. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul pleaded three times for his thorn to be removed. God refused, but gave grace and a promise: his power is made perfect in weakness. Paul learned to boast in his weaknesses. A refused prayer became a gateway to a deeper experience of Christ's strength.

verseByVerse.quote: Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples, "Sit here, while I go over there and pray." And taking with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be sorrowful and troubled. Then he said to them, "My soul is very sorrowful, even to death; remain here, and watch with me." And going a little farther he fell on his face and prayed, saying, "My Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will." And he came to the disciples and found them sleeping. And he said to Peter, "So, could you not watch with me one hour? Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak." Again, for the second time, he went away and prayed, "My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, your will be done." And again he came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy. So, leaving them again, he went away and prayed for the third time, saying the same words again. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus prayed three times in Gethsemane that the cup might pass. Each time he submitted: your will be done. The Father did not remove the cup. Because of that unanswered request, salvation was accomplished. Jesus models honest prayer and complete submission.

verseByVerse.quote: And he told them a parable to the effect that they ought always to pray and not lose heart. He said, "In a certain city there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected man. And there was a widow in that city who kept coming to him and saying, 'Give me justice against my adversary.' For a while he refused, but afterward he said to himself, 'Though I neither fear God nor respect man, yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will give her justice, so that she will not beat me down by her continual coming.'" And the Lord said, "Hear what the unrighteous judge says. And will not God give justice to his elect, who cry to him day and night? Will he delay long over them? I tell you, he will give justice to them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth?" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus told a parable about a persistent widow and an unjust judge. If an unjust judge eventually gives justice, how much more will God give justice to his elect who cry to him day and night? Jesus encourages perseverance in prayer, and asks whether he will find faith on earth when he comes.

verseByVerse.quote: Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what to pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words. And he who searches hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God. And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose. For those whom he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, in order that he might be the firstborn among many brothers. And those whom he predestined he also called, and those whom he called he also justified, and those whom he justified he also glorified. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Spirit helps us when we do not know how to pray, interceding for us according to God's will. God works all things for good for those who love him. His purpose is to conform us to the image of his Son, and he will bring every one of his people to glory. Unanswered prayers are part of that good purpose.

4.reflection:
Which unanswered prayer has been hardest for you?

How does Jesus' prayer in Gethsemane help you understand unanswered prayer?

What is the difference between "no," "wait" and "a different answer"?

How does Romans 8:28-29 help you trust God when prayers are not answered as you hoped?

5.title: Strengthening Faith
5.overview:
Faith is a gift from God, but it can be strengthened. Scripture shows how.

Hear God's word. So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ (Rom 10:17). Faith grows as we read, hear and meditate on Scripture. The Gospels were written so that you may believe (John 20:31). Doubters should not stop reading the Bible; they should read it more.

Look to Jesus. Looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith (Heb 12:2). Faith grows by looking at its object, not by examining itself. The more we see of Christ, his character, his cross, his resurrection, the more we trust him.

Remember God's faithfulness. Israel built memorials to remember what God had done (Josh 4). Remembering God's past faithfulness in Scripture and in our own lives strengthens faith for the present.

Stay in fellowship. Believers strengthen one another. The writer of Hebrews lists the heroes of faith in chapter 11, then says, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us run with endurance (Heb 12:1). The faith of others, past and present, encourages ours.

Obey what you know. Faith grows through obedience. When we step out in trust, we see God's faithfulness, and our faith grows.

Pray for faith. The apostles asked Jesus, Increase our faith! (Luke 17:5). It is right to ask God for stronger faith.

Rest in assurance. John wrote, I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life (1 John 5:13). God wants his children to be sure. Our security rests not on our grip on Christ but on his grip on us: no one will snatch them out of my hand (John 10:28).
5.theology:
Faith is a gift: For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God (Eph 2:8). We do not manufacture faith. We receive it and ask for more.

Tested faith: Peter says trials come so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold that perishes though it is tested by fire—may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ (1 Pet 1:7). Doubt and testing can refine faith.

Christ intercedes: Jesus prayed for Peter that his faith would not fail (Luke 22:32). He prays for his people still (Heb 7:25). Our faith is upheld by his intercession.
5.examples:
Then: Hebrews 11 lists people who trusted God's promises without seeing them fulfilled: Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Moses and many more. These all died in faith, not having received the things promised (Heb 11:13). Their example still strengthens believers who wait.

Now: A man struggling with doubts begins to read one Gospel chapter every morning, asking, "What does this show me about Jesus?" He also keeps a list of answered prayers and God's kindnesses. Over a year, his faith steadies. His questions have not all been answered, but his trust in Christ is stronger.

A simple test: Which of these ways of strengthening faith could you practise this week?

verseByVerse.quote: How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching? And how are they to preach unless they are sent? As it is written, "How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news!" But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed what he has heard from us?" So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul traces a chain: people cannot call on someone they have not believed in, believe in someone they have not heard of, or hear without a preacher. Faith comes by hearing the word of Christ. The word of God is the ordinary means by which faith is born and grows.

verseByVerse.quote: Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen. For by it the people of old received their commendation. By faith we understand that the universe was created by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible. By faith Abel offered to God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain, through which he was commended as righteous, God commending him by accepting his gifts. And through his faith, though he died, he still speaks. By faith Enoch was taken up so that he should not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him. Now before he was taken he was commended as having pleased God. And without faith it is impossible to please him, for whoever would draw near to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for and the conviction of things not seen. By faith we understand creation. Without faith it is impossible to please God, because whoever comes to him must believe that he exists and rewards those who seek him. Faith seeks God.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is seated at the right hand of the throne of God. Consider him who endured from sinners such hostility against himself, so that you may not grow weary or fainthearted. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The great cloud of witnesses encourages us to run with endurance. But the main focus is Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who endured the cross for the joy set before him. Consider him, so that you will not grow weary or fainthearted.

verseByVerse.quote: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father's hand. I and the Father are one." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus' sheep hear his voice, and he knows them. He gives them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of his hand or his Father's hand. The security of believers rests on the power and promise of Christ, not on the steadiness of their feelings.

5.reflection:
Which means of strengthening faith do you most neglect?

How does "looking to Jesus" (Heb 12:2) differ from looking at your own faith?

Make a list of ways God has been faithful to you. How does it affect your faith?

Read John 10:27-30. How does it comfort you in times of doubt?
